title: MeCP2 MBD-ID module: a unified DNA/RNA binding interface disrupted in Rett syndrome.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unzipped the Europe PMC supplementary package (1.18 MB) and extracted all 14 pages of the only data file, gkag890_supplemental_file.pdf. Counted its contents: Table S1 lists 9 recombinant protein sequences, Table S2 lists 19 DNA/RNA oligonucleotides, Table S3 lists 4 mutagenesis primer pairs, Table S4 holds 6 rows of apparent dissociation constants (binding strengths) in nanomolar; the remaining pages are gel and binding-curve figures (S1-S4). Also pulled the full open-access text and read Table 1 directly: 7 protein constructs x 3 nucleic-acid ligands = 21 binding-strength values. Counted every '+/-' in the whole article text: 27 occurrences total, i.e. fewer than ~60 measured values exist anywhere.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The experimental detail of how each binding strength was measured (fluorescence anisotropy and gel-shift assays, n>3 replicates) comes from the methods section. The claim that no numeric source file was deposited rests on the data availability statement ('available in the article and in its online supplementary material') plus the absence of any repository accession in the Europe PMC accession scan and in a Zenodo/Dryad search on the DOI.

a1_downloadable.note: The supplementary PDF (0.76 MB) and all figures download freely from Europe PMC with no login. But it is a PDF only: no CSV, TSV or spreadsheet, and no deposited raw binding curves, so every number would have to be typed in by hand.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The prediction target (KD,app, the apparent binding strength in nanomolar) is printed as a value in Table 1 and Supplementary Table S4, so it exists as a reported measurement rather than something to be inferred. It is in PDF cells, not a data column, which is transcription work, not construction.

a3_inputs_present.note: Verified in Table S1 and S2: full amino-acid sequences for all 9 protein constructs and full 5'-3' sequences for all 19 DNA/RNA ligands, including methylated-cytosine positions, are written out. No accession lookups needed.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are explicit and consistent throughout: KD,app in nanomolar (nM) in both tables, with micromolar (uM) used only for the weak MBD-alone and ID-alone interactions, and the RNA melting temperature in degrees Celsius.

a5_enough_rows.note: KILLER. Counted in the files, not read from the paper: Table 1 gives 21 binding-strength values (7 protein constructs x 3 ligands), Supplementary Table S4 adds 6 rows which largely restate the same pairs by a second assay, and a count of every '+/-' in the whole article text returns 27 measured values in total. The checklist needs ~1,500 labelled rows, or ~400 for classification; this is roughly 25-60 measurements depending on how you count, i.e. 25-50x too few. The experimental unit is a protein-construct/ligand pair, and there are only 9 constructs and 19 ligands, so even a complete grid would be bounded well under 200.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially fits; the entire dataset is one small PDF. Not scored further because A5 already fails.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Table 1 in the text and Table S4 in the supplement agree with each other within the stated error bars for the overlapping protein-ligand pairs (for example MBD-ID versus methylated BDNF DNA: 2.7 +/- 0.9 nM in Table 1, 3 +/- 1 nM in Table S4).

a8_label_provenance.note: The labels are real physical measurements, not another model's output: apparent binding strengths fitted from fluorescence anisotropy titrations and confirmed by gel-shift and competition assays, with at least 3 independent replicates. Not computable from the input sequences, so no leakage by construction. Provenance is clean; the problem is purely how few of them there are.

honest_claim_h3: No honest model claim is possible: with roughly 27 measured binding strengths spanning 9 protein constructs, any fitted model would be describing seven mutants of one protein domain rather than learning how sequence changes alter nucleic-acid binding.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use protein and nucleic-acid sequence to predict how tightly a MeCP2 fragment grips methylated DNA or structured RNA.
plain_idea.train_on: The project considered would show the model a protein construct's amino-acid sequence plus a DNA or RNA ligand sequence (with methylated cytosines marked). I verified only 9 protein sequences and 19 ligand sequences exist here, giving roughly 27 measured pairs, which is far too few.
plain_idea.predict: The output would be the apparent dissociation constant KD,app in nanomolar, i.e. the concentration at which half the protein is bound. The true values come from fluorescence anisotropy titrations, cross-checked by gel-shift and competition assays, done in this one laboratory.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups engineering MeCP2 'MiniGene' therapies for Rett syndrome would want to know in advance whether a shortened construct keeps its RNA binding, since this paper shows the MiniGene loses more than 5-fold RNA affinity. With 27 measurements, though, nothing can be learned by modelling that the paper's own table does not already say outright.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: predict apparent binding strength (KD,app) of MeCP2 protein fragments against methylated DNA, unmethylated DNA and structured RNA from the protein and ligand sequences, with a protein language model such as ESM-2 providing the protein representation. Dead on arrival because the dataset is a 7-construct x 3-ligand table. The only salvageable fragment of an idea is to use these 21-27 values as a tiny held-out biophysical test set for a model trained elsewhere, which is a validation footnote, not a project.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: hand-transcribing two PDF tables into a CSV is about two hours, and embedding 9 short protein sequences with a small ESM-2 checkpoint on a laptop CPU takes minutes. Compute was never the constraint here; sample size is.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the dissociation constants in Table 1 and Supplementary Table S4. That took one extraction of the supplementary PDF and returned 21 and 6 values respectively, against a 1,500-row requirement.

verdict_reason: A5 fails by a wide margin, verified in the files: roughly 27 measured binding strengths across 9 protein constructs and 19 nucleic-acid ligands, all printed in PDF tables with no deposited numeric data. This is an elegant single-protein biophysics study whose entire dataset fits on one page; the labels are clean, measured and properly unit-stated, but there is no dataset here to model.
